summary: Our project utilizes a precise RAG (Retrival Augmented Generation) that extracts data that we were given through project resources. With this RAG and our Ollama link, we developed a machine (ULTRAKILL REFERENCE HAHAHAHAHHA) that allows you to inquire about the known data and give conditions to predict and rank flammability outcomes. This addresses the challenge by acknowledging the importance of how future missions, the more we progress, missions grow longer. This means that unknown factors may play into dangerous scenarios that may end up abolishing life on the spacecraft and destroying everything that has been worked for. Our machine can predict whether something is flammable under conditions in space and earth allowing us to strategically place fire sensors where flammable areas are or change material to make them less or non flammable. Thus we must focus on keeping the spacecraft and our everyday lives on earth safer, through FIRE DATA.
details: To run this project, please read the README folder when installed. We have 4 pieces in PROJECT Fire Data. The AI chat, fire physics engine, safety insights, and a page for showing what sources were used in the creation of this project. This allows us to see the possibiliies outcome before we even start, allowing us to create the perfect environment that reduces the dangers regarding fire outbreaks. This project is not only for determining possibilities of flammable dangers in space but also on earth as well. "Similarly, some NASA technology has led to improvements in intellectual smoke detection and firefighter gear, including protective gear, air tank, etc." (Alice Chien, NASA Spaceapps flames in freefall challenge video), this quote shows that the NASA technology has already created innovations in protection against fire and with our project, we wish to push these protections further using simulations that are connected to NASA experiment data. We used HTML, JS, CSS, and Python. Our project is creative as we put our AI use to a minimum while developing this project so that our own creativity was shown compared to all the other projects that we have witnessed. Our team considered factors such as how useful it is to the scientists that use our product and we also considered how easy it is to understand so we made it simple so that anyone can understand at a glance.
